verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              य इमे पृथिवीपालाः शेरते पृथिवीतले । पृतनामध्य एते हि गतसंज्ञा महाबलाः ॥१॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said These kings who lie on the Earth's surface amid their respective armies, these princes of great power, are now all deprived of life.

verses.sanskrit: एकैकशो भीमबला नागायुतबलास्तथा । एते हि निहताः संख्ये तुल्यतेजोबलैर्नरैः ॥२॥
verses.english: Every one of these powerful kings was endued with strength equal to that of ten thousand elephants. Alas! these have all have killed by men equally powerful and strong.

verses.sanskrit: नैषां पश्यामि हन्तारं प्राणिनां संयुगे परम् । विक्रमेणोपसम्पन्नास्तेजोबलसमन्विताः ॥३॥
verses.english: I do not see any one else that could kill any of these men in battle. All of them were gifted with great prowess, great energy, and great strength.

verses.sanskrit: अथ चेमे महाप्राज्ञाः शेरते हि गतासवः । मृता इति च शब्दोऽयं वर्तत्येषु गतासुषु ॥४॥
verses.english: Highly wise, they are now lying dead on the naked earth. about them, however, that are deprived of life, the word that is used is that they are dead.

verses.sanskrit: इमे मृता नृपतयः प्रायशो भीमविक्रमाः । तत्र मे संशयो जातः कुतः संज्ञा मृता इति ॥५॥
verses.english: All these highly powerful kings are said to be dead. On this subject a doubt lies in my mind. Whence is life and whence is death.

verses.sanskrit: कस्य मृत्युः कुतो मृत्युः केन मृत्युरिह प्रजाः । हरत्यमरसंकाश तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥६॥
verses.english: Who is it that dies? whence is death? Whence is death? Why does death take away living creatures. O grandfather, tell me this, O you who are like a god.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              पुरा कृतयुगे तात राजा ह्यासीदकम्पनः । स शत्रुवशमापन्नः संग्रामे क्षीणवाहनः ॥७॥
verses.english: Bhishma said In days of yore, in the Krita age, O son, there was a king of the name of Anukampaka. His cars, elephants, horse and men having been reduced in number, he succumbed to the power of his enemies in battle.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य पुत्रो हरिर्नाम नारायणसमो बले । स शत्रुभिर्हतः संख्ये सबलः सपदानुगः ॥८॥
verses.english: His son, named Hari, who was like Narayana himself in strength, was in that battle killed by his enemies along with all his followers and troops.

verses.sanskrit: स राजा शत्रुवशगः पुत्रशोकसमन्वितः । यदृच्छया शान्तिपरो ददर्श भुवि नारदम् ॥९॥
verses.english: Stricken with grief consequent on the death of his son, and himself brought under the control of enemies, the king devoted himself thence to a life of peacefulness. One day, while wandering listlessly he met the sage Narada on the Earth.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मै स सर्वमाचष्ट यथावृत्तं जनेश्वरः । शत्रुाभिर्ग्रहणं संख्ये पुत्रस्य मरणं तथा ॥१०॥
verses.english: The king told Narada all that had taken place, viz., the death of his son in battle and his own capture by his enemies.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा नारदोऽथ तपोधनः । आख्यानमिदमाचष्ट पुत्रशोकापहं तदा ॥११॥
verses.english: Having heard him Narada, endued with wealth of penances, then recited to him the following narrative for removing his grief consequent on the death of his son.

verses.sanskrit:
नारद उवाच।
              राजन् शृणु समाख्यानमद्येदं बहुविस्तरम् । यथावृत्तं श्रुतं चैव मयेदं वसुधाधिप ॥१२॥
verses.english: Narada said Listen now, O king, to the following long narrative which had taken place. I myself heard it formerly, O king!

verses.sanskrit: प्रजाः सृष्टाः महातेजाः प्रजासर्गे पितामहः । अतीव वृद्धा बहुला नामृष्यत पुनः प्रजाः ॥१३॥
verses.english: Endued with great energy, the Grandfather, at the time of the creation of the universe, created a large number of living beings. These multiplied greatly, and none of them died.

verses.sanskrit: न ह्यन्तरमभूत्किञ्चित्क्वचिज्जन्तुभिरच्युत । निरुच्छ्वासमिवोन्नद्धं त्रैलोक्यमभवन्नृप ॥१४॥
verses.english: There was not a part of the universe which was not overcrowded with living creatures, O you of great glory! Indeed, O king, the three worlds appeared to swell with living beings, and became, as it were, breathless.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य चिन्ता समुत्पन्ना संहारं प्रति भूपते । चिन्तयन्नाध्यगच्छच्च संहारे हेतुकारणम् ॥१५॥
verses.english: Then, O king, the Grandfather thought as to how he should destroy the surplus population. Thinking of the matter, the Self-create, however, could not decide by what means the destruction of life was to be performed.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य रोषान्महाराज खेभ्योऽग्निरुदतिष्ठत । तेन सर्वा दिशो राजन् ददाह स पितामहः ॥१६॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O king, Brahman gave way to anger and in consequence of his anger a fire issued out of his body. With that fire born of his anger, the Grandfather burnt all the quarters of the universe, O king.

verses.sanskrit: ततो दिवं भुवं खं च जगच्च सचराचरम् । ददाह पावको राजन् भगवत्कोपसम्भवः ॥१७॥
verses.english: Indeed, that fire begotten of the Divine Lord's anger, O king, burnt Heaven and Earth and the Sky and the whole Universe with all its mobile and immobile beings.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रादह्यन्त भूतानि जङ्गमानि ध्रुवाणि च । महता क्रोधवेगेन कुपिते प्रपितामहे ॥१८॥
verses.english: Truly, when the Grandfather thus became angry, all mobile and immobile beings began to be consumed by the irresistible power of that anger.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽध्वरजटः स्थाणुर्वेदाध्वरपतिः शिवः । जगाम शरणं देवो ब्रह्माणं परवीरहा ॥१९॥
verses.english: Then the divine and sacred Sthanu, that destroyer of hostile heroes, that lord of the Vedas and the scriptures, filled with pity, tried to please Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन्नभिगते स्थाणौ प्रजानां हितकाम्यया । अब्रवीत्परमो देवो ज्वलन्निव तदा शिवम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: When Sthanu came to Brahma out of feelings of benevolence, the great God addressed him, saying,-you deserved boons at my hands! What desire of yours shall I fulfil? I shall do you good by doing whatever you wish.

verses.sanskrit: करवाण्यद्य कं कामं वरार्होऽसि मतो मम । कर्ता ह्यस्मि प्रियं शम्भो तव यद्धृदि वर्तते ॥२१॥
